newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-FORMER CHAMPIONS HELP LAUNCH NEW SHOW-COURT.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-FORMER CHAMPIONS HELP LAUNCH NEW SHOW-COURT.

text.p: Wimbledon's greatest champions did their best to steal local favourite Tim Henman's limelight on Monday as showers delayed the first competitive action on the All England Club's new Number One court.
The official opening of the new show court went ahead as scheduled under threatening skies, with several of tennis's most famous names adding some glamour to the occasion.

But with the formalities over, there was not even time for a single shot in the opening match between Henman and Canadian Daniel Nestor before rain forced the players to hurry back to the locker-rooms.

It was an anti-climax for many fans who had queued all night on the pavement to ensure a glimpse of the British number one, the focus of what has become known as "Henmania" since he made the last eight at Wimbledon last year.

Their consolation, though, was a close-up view of 10 former champions who were all presented with a silver salver before the Duke of Kent, president of the All England Club, officially declared the new court open.

Rod Laver, John Newcombe, John McEnroe, Boris Becker and Pete Sampras were joined by their female counterparts Louise Brough, Margaret Court, Billie Jean King, Chris Evert and Martina Navratilova in a lap of honour around the 11,000-capacity arena.

Newcombe almost provided some unscheduled entertainment when he accidentally stumbled on the edge of the red carpet as he walked over to collect his salver, while McEnroe raised a laugh by feigning surprise when he was introduced as the man who had introduced a new phrase into the English language.

The American's trademark lament -- "You cannot be serious" -- seemed particularly appropriate when the showers arrived to spoil Henman's entrance, but the players were eventually able to start after a half-hour delay.

If the championships do turn out to be badly affected by the weather, it will re-open the debate as to whether the new court should have included a retractable roof, similar to the one used at the Australian Open in Melbourne.
The foundations are in place to support such a structure but the All England Club say they have no plans to install one.
